**Fly through the ground into caves with Ghost.** 3D Sculpt's Player has a third way to move beside Walking and Flying: **Ghost**, chosen at the bottom right of the view or with G (its key can be changed in Settings ▸ Keyboard), flies through everything, as the game's spectator mode does, to go into caves, under overhangs and along tunnels and sculpt or paint there. With your eyes in the ground the view sees through it, its edges darkened and **In the ground** said in the bar, to the air beyond and the walls and floor of the caves there, and the cursor and the brush work on the surface shown. The flight speed is Ghost's too; G again flies out, from the first air above if you are in the ground.

**3D Sculpt works with the tools of the Tools panel.** Its own Sculpt, Smooth and Paint buttons are gone: it uses the tool chosen in the Tools panel, with its Tool Settings and Brush Settings, exactly as the map does, and its workspace now shows those three panels beside the view. Raise / Lower sculpts in 3D at its own speed, into overhangs and caves; Smooth smooths exactly as on the map (the same heights from the same stroke, the brush's shape, a stamp too, only shaping its falloff), its outline laid on the land over exactly the columns it takes, where it used to mark a different, jagged shape and leave the slopes in steps; Paint terrain paints the columns and the matter sculpted there; the Gradient brush, Paint biome, covers, objects, the other layers and the height tools act on the columns where the cursor points, and the Eyedropper, Flood and Drain where you click. A tool of the map only, a selection shape say, says so at the top of the view, where the buttons then turn and move the view. The top of the view names the tool in hand and the bar along the bottom of the player's view lists what its buttons do. A 3D Sculpt workspace laid out before gets the new panels once, unless you had given it the Tools panel yourself.
